findings.title: Async calendar/video deletions in forEach are never awaited
findings.body: In packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts the code does bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...)/deleteMeeting(...); }). Array.forEach does not await async callbacks, so the deletions run fire-and-forget. The surrounding try/catch cannot catch their rejections, and the function proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true immediately. Consequence is orphaned events on external calendars/video providers on failure and unhandled promise rejections. Use Promise.all or for...of with await.

The surrounding try/catch cannot catch their rejections, and the function proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true immediately. findings.title: Reschedule deletions fired in forEach without awaiting
findings.body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx requestReschedule does bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...)/deleteMeeting(...); }) and then immediately sends reschedule email and webhooks without awaiting. Because forEach never awaits the async callback, calendar/video deletions may not have started or finished, errors are lost as unhandled rejections, and the previous time slot may stay blocked. Collect promises and await Promise.all.

findings.title: Recurring cancel pushes to apiDeletes from unawaited forEach
findings.body: In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts recurring cancellation does bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); for (...) apiDeletes.push(await calendar?.deleteEvent(...)); }). The outer forEach is not awaited, but apiDeletes is later consumed by Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)). Because the pushes happen asynchronously after the await of getCalendar, Promise.all can run with an incomplete apiDeletes list, so some recurring calendar deletions are silently skipped and errors inside are uncaught. Use for...of with await or await Promise.all of mapped promises.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials now stores a Promise as calendar but stays sync
findings.body: In packages/core/CalendarManager.ts getCalendarCredentials does const calendar = getCalendar(credential) after getCalendar became async, so calendar is Promise<Calendar|null>, not Calendar|null. The function remains synchronous and returns objects with a promise in the calendar field. Only getConnectedCalendars was patched to do await item.calendar. Any other consumer expecting a Calendar will get a Promise (e.g., calling listCalendars/createEvent on it fails), and the return type is now misleading. Make getCalendarCredentials async and resolve calendars before returning.

findings.title: getVideoAdapters serializes independent dynamic imports
findings.body: In packages/core/videoClient.ts getVideoAdapters loops for (const cred of withCredentials) { const app = await appStore[...]; ... } which awaits each dynamic import sequentially. The imports are independent, so latency adds up, notably for getBusyVideoTimes and availability paths with multiple video credentials. Use Promise.all to load adapters in parallel.
